Laura — drafting alternatives below. Kept both short so procurement can compare quickly. Please note I recommend keeping IP/data obligations outside the exclusion and limiting the cap ask.

Option A — One-way (Redwood-favored):
""
Except for liability arising from a party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, infringement of a party's intellectual property rights, or a breach of Section X (Data Security and Privacy), NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, EXEMPLARY OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS, LOSS OF DATA, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, WHETHER BASED IN CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY OR OTHER THEORIES OF LIABILITY.

THE AGGREGATE LIABILITY OF REDWOOD ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID BY CUSTOMER TO REDWOOD UNDER THE APPLICABLE ORDER FORM IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.
""

Option B — Mutual (customer-favored but with carvebacks):
""
EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING FROM A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT, INTENTIONAL MISUSE OF CUSTOMER DATA, OR A BREACH OF SECTION X (DATA SECURITY AND PRIVACY), NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, EXEMPLARY OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES. FOR CLARITY, CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SHALL NOT INCLUDE DIRECT LOSS OF REVENUE OR DIRECT COSTS INCURRED TO REMEDIATE A BREACH.

THE AGGREGATE LIABILITY OF EACH PARTY FOR DIRECT DAMAGES ARISING UNDER OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID BY CUSTOMER TO REDWOOD UNDER THE APPLICABLE ORDER FORM IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.
""

Notes: 
- If ACME insists on mutual, we should explicitly exclude IP and data torts from the exclusion and add the carveback language so they can't recategorize direct losses as consequential.
- Cap at 12 months of fees is defensible. We usually start at 6 months for smaller pilots; given enterprise scale here, 12 months is reasonable if we tie it to customer’s order form fees and keep the exceptions tight.

If you want, I can send Option B with tracked changes to ACME with a short cover note.

-Markus

--

1) Replace "DIRECT LOSS OF REVENUE" with "DIRECT LOSS OF REVENUE OR DIRECT LOSS OF BUSINESS" to avoid ACME trying to relabel channel impacts as direct.
2) Add sentence: "For clarity, costs to investigate or remediate a data security incident shall be considered direct damages where such costs arise from Redwood's breach of its obligations under Section X." This preserves customer protection for incident remediation but keeps general "remediation costs" out of the carveback.
